About me

With more than six years behind a camera and a drone in Vientiane, I work across video creation, aerial cinematography and photography — for banks, insurers, studios and brands. Every frame is built with intention: precise, cinematic, and made to be felt. Let's build something worth watching.

Kaopoon Studio · Vientiane

Services

01
Video Creation

Concept to final delivery — promotional films, documentaries, social campaigns and corporate storytelling, cut and graded to your brand's vision.

02
Drone Cinematography

Licensed aerial operations across Laos and Southeast Asia, delivering sweeping cinematic movement no ground camera can reach.

03
Photography & Retouching

Portrait, event, product and landscape work with a sharp eye for composition and natural light — every image retouched and colour graded.

04
Motion Graphics

Titles, lower thirds, logo animation and animated ads that give campaigns rhythm and keep a brand recognisable in motion.

05
AI Content Production

AI-assisted image and video generation folded into a real production pipeline — faster concepts, more looks tested, the same finish quality.

Project

01
Documentary · Aerial · Event — 2026
CARBS Sayaboury
Field Production

Full visual documentation for the Climate Adaptive River Basins of Sayaboury programme — aerial mapping of the river basin, village livelihood photography, on-location interview portraits and coverage of the MoU signing and inception workshop. Shot across Sayaboury province, August 2026.

02
Documentary · Aerial · Portraits — 2026
Phou Xieng Thong NPA
Field Production

Three days on the Mekong documenting the Phou Xieng Thong National Protected Area — dawn aerials over the river cliffs, fishermen casting nets from longtail boats, ranger and patrol-team portraits, village livelihoods and community consultation meetings. June 2026.

Behind
the scenes

Most of what ends up on screen starts here — a tripod in the sand, a boat that leaves before sunrise, an interview set up under whatever shade is available. From the Mekong at Phou Xieng Thong to the river basins of Sayaboury to a rural classroom and the studio floor at Kaopoon — this is how the work actually gets made.
